body_markdown:
**By Lisha Ma, Marketing Manager**


Trade shows are often measured by booth traffic, lead counts, or product launches. While those metrics matter, my biggest takeaway from the 2026 China International Industry Fair (CIIF) was something far more valuable: the quality of the conversations we had with customers.


This year, we hosted the largest[Robotics & Automation](https://novanta.com/robotics-automation/) booth in our CIIF history. While the expanded space allowed us to showcase more technologies, the real value came from the insights customers shared with us.


Many conversations started at one of our eight robotic workstations but quickly moved beyond the technology itself. Customers wanted to discuss production goals, implementation challenges, accuracy requirements, cycle times, workforce pressures, and future automation plans.


That was exactly our objective.


The workstations were built around two themes: how six-axis[force/torque sensors](https://novanta.com/robotics-automation/products/force-torque-sensors/) enable advanced automation applications and how[tool changers](https://ati.novanta.com/products/tool-changers/) create greater flexibility in manufacturing environments. Through demonstrations ranging from gear assembly and automotive inspection to[surgical robotics](https://novanta.com/robotics-automation/application/surgical/) and new energy applications, we focused on showing technologies at work in real production scenarios.


The approach resonated with visitors. Demonstrations such as force-controlled gear assembly, automated tightening-gun switching, and force-controlled surgical robotics generated strong interest, but what stood out most was how quickly conversations shifted from products to applications.


Instead of asking what the product could do, customers wanted to understand whether it would work in their application and help solve their manufacturing challenges.


Those questions led to discussions about implementation, integration, expected outcomes, and business goals. They also reflected a broader trend across manufacturing: Companies are looking beyond individual components and seeking practical solutions that improve quality, productivity, and flexibility without adding unnecessary complexity.


### **The Conversations Behind the Technology**


For our marketing team, the most valuable outcome of CIIF was the opportunity to better understand what customers are trying to achieve.


Throughout the event, our Robotics & Automation specialists, sales professionals, and application engineers worked together to explore customer requirements, challenges, and opportunities. These conversations provided valuable insight into emerging automation needs across industries and regions while helping customers identify practical paths forward.


Through the eight workstations, we showcased new possibilities for force/torque sensing and flexible automation. Just as importantly, we gathered feedback, uncovered new opportunities, and strengthened relationships with customers exploring their next automation investments.


As we follow up on the needs and application questions identified during the show, our focus remains the same: helping customers move from possibility to implementation with solutions designed around their real-world challenges.
